# realtime

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D4 Backend & APIs (BE)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** MDN, "EventSource" (SSE, Last-Event-ID) — https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/EventSource ; MDN, "WebSocket" — https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/WebSocket
- **Depends on:** backend-auth, queues-jobs
- **Feeds into:** notifications, frontend-state

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** the product must push changes to clients as they happen — status feeds, notifications, progress, chat, collaboration, presence — and the transport, authentication, and reconnect behavior are being designed.
- **Do NOT use when:** data changes rarely and a fetch on view is honest; not everything deserves a socket. Do not present polling as a realtime implementation — polling is a labeled degraded fallback (BE-211), never the design.

## Rules

1. **BE-201 — Transport matches direction.** Server→client streams (feeds, notifications, progress) use server-sent events. Bidirectional traffic (chat, collaboration) uses WebSocket. The choice is recorded with its reason.
2. **BE-202 — Authenticate at the handshake.** Connections authenticate during the handshake, with the session cookie or a short-lived token. A long-lived credential never appears in a connection URL, where it would be logged and shared.
3. **BE-203 — Authorize per channel.** A client may subscribe only to channels its identity is authorized for, checked at subscribe time. Tenant channels are scoped to the tenant; a client-supplied channel name is a request, not a grant.
4. **BE-204 — Re-check on change.** When a user's permissions or tenant membership change, their live subscriptions are re-evaluated and unauthorized channels are dropped. Connecting once does not grant a stream forever.
5. **BE-205 — Events carry IDs.** Every event has an ID and a per-channel sequence number, so a reconnecting client can prove exactly what it missed.
6. **BE-206 — Reconnect is part of the protocol.** Clients reconnect with exponential backoff and jitter, then catch up from the last event ID (e.g. `Last-Event-ID`) or receive an explicit resync signal. A silent gap is a defect.
7. **BE-207 — Heartbeats both ways.** Connections heartbeat on an interval; peers that stop answering are detected and closed, so presence and fan-out never target ghosts.
8. **BE-208 — A backplane beyond one instance.** Once more than one instance serves traffic, fan-out runs through a pub/sub backplane (for example Redis). Per-process subscription memory is a single-instance trap.
9. **BE-209 — Backpressure is capped.** Slow consumers get a bounded buffer. Past the cap, the consumer is dropped with a resync signal — never allowed to grow server memory without limit.
10. **BE-210 — Live means live.** Presence, typing indicators, and "live" figures derive from real connection and event state. Nothing time-based or randomized renders as live.
11. **BE-211 — The degraded mode is designed.** On hosts that restrict long-lived connections, the fallback (SSE-only, then polling) is implemented, labeled in the UI as delayed where it is, and tested — not improvised during an outage.

## BAN list

- **BAN-BE-101 — Polling dressed as realtime.** Banned: a `setInterval` poll presented to users as "real-time" or "live" sync. Defeats: DET-FAKE-022. Instead: push over SSE or WebSocket (BE-201); if polling is the fallback, label the state "delayed" (BE-211). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-BE-102 — Timer-driven live indicators.** Banned: viewer counts, presence dots, or "someone is typing" rendered from timers or random drift with no connection or event source behind them. Defeats: DET-FAKE-018. Instead: derive every live indicator from the connection registry and real events (BE-210). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-BE-103 — Unauthenticated connections.** Banned: accepting a socket or SSE connection with no handshake authentication, or carrying a long-lived API key in the connection URL. Defeats: DET-CODE-020. Instead: authenticate at the handshake with the session cookie or a short-lived, single-purpose token (BE-202). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-BE-104 — Open channel subscription.** Banned: honoring any client-supplied channel name without an authorization check, so any client can subscribe to another tenant's stream. Defeats: DET-FAKE-021. Instead: check the subscription against the identity's authorized channels at subscribe time (BE-203). Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-BE-101 — Two-session live update test.** Verifies: BE-201, BE-210. Check: automated — open two authenticated sessions; perform an action in one and assert the other reflects it via the realtime channel, with no refresh and no polling requests in the network log. Pass: the update arrives over the stream. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-BE-102 — Drop-and-reconnect test.** Verifies: BE-205, BE-206. Check: automated — connect, note the last event ID, force a disconnect, emit three events, reconnect. Pass: the client receives exactly the three missed events, or one explicit resync — no gaps, no duplicates. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-BE-103 — Connection authorization test.** Verifies: BE-202, BE-203. Check: automated — attempt a connection with no credentials, with expired credentials, and subscribe a tenant-A client to a tenant-B channel. Pass: all three rejected. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-BE-104 — Slow-consumer test.** Verifies: BE-209. Check: automated — connect a client that never reads, publish past the buffer cap, and observe. Pass: the server drops the consumer with a resync signal and server memory stays bounded. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- Direction picks the transport: SSE one-way, WebSocket two-way.
- Authenticate at the handshake; authorize every channel.
- Events carry IDs; reconnect means catch up or resync — never a gap.
- Presence is connection state, not a timer.
- Past one instance, fan-out needs a backplane.

## Checklist

- [ ] The transport matches the traffic direction; polling is only a labeled fallback (BE-201).
- [ ] Two-session test: updates arrive over the stream, with no polling (G-BE-101).
- [ ] Drop-and-reconnect: no missed or duplicated events (G-BE-102).
- [ ] Unauthenticated, expired, and cross-tenant attempts are all rejected (G-BE-103).
- [ ] A slow consumer is dropped with a resync signal; memory stays bounded (G-BE-104).
- [ ] Live indicators read connection and event state only (BE-210).
- [ ] A pub/sub backplane is configured wherever more than one instance runs (BE-208).

# rest-conventions

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D4 Backend & APIs (BE)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** Zalando RESTful API Guidelines — http://opensource.zalando.com/restful-api-guidelines/ ; RFC 9110 HTTP semantics summary — https://apiguide.dev/specifications/http-semantics
- **Depends on:** api-architecture, api-versioning
- **Feeds into:** api-building, api-documentation, sdk-design

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** designing new endpoints, reviewing an API surface for consistency, or writing the project's convention sheet — paths, methods, status codes, pagination, casing, and versioning all follow one written convention.
- **Do NOT use when:** implementing a single handler's internals (api-building), formatting error bodies in depth (error-handling), or validating payloads (validation). This skill fixes the shape of the surface; other skills build behind it.

## Rules

1. **BE-021 — One convention sheet per API.** Before endpoints are added, the API has a written convention sheet derived from RFC 9110 semantics and one published style guide. The sheet is enforced by linting the OpenAPI document in CI, not by memory.
2. **BE-022 — Resources are plural noun collections.** Paths name resources (`/orders`, `/users/{id}/orders`), in kebab-case, nested only where ownership is real. A path segment names a thing, never an action.
3. **BE-023 — No verbs in URLs.** Non-CRUD actions are modeled as sub-resources (`POST /orders/{id}/cancellations`) or, where the chosen guide prescribes it, `POST /orders/{id}:cancel`. `POST /cancelOrder` is never acceptable.
4. **BE-024 — Methods keep their RFC 9110 meaning.** GET is safe and side-effect-free; PUT replaces the whole resource; PATCH modifies part of it; DELETE removes it. Repeating a PUT or DELETE lands on the same end state.
5. **BE-025 — Status codes follow the decision rule.** `201` + `Location` on create, `204` on empty success, `400` malformed, `409` state conflict, `412` precondition failed, `422` business-rule rejection. An error is never returned with `200`.
6. **BE-026 — One pagination style, from day one.** Every list endpoint paginates — cursor preferred for large or fast-changing collections — with a documented maximum page size. Retrofitting pagination later breaks clients that assumed complete results.
7. **BE-027 — One casing and query grammar.** One field-casing rule for JSON bodies, and one filtering/sorting grammar (`?status=open&sort=-createdAt` style) applies to every endpoint in the API.
8. **BE-028 — Released versions are never silently mutated.** The major version appears in the path only when a breaking change ships, and a superseded version gets an announced deprecation window before removal.
9. **BE-029 — Evolution is additive or it is a new major.** Adding optional fields or new endpoints is compatible evolution; removing, renaming, or re-typing a field is breaking and follows BE-028.
10. **BE-030 — Errors are problem details everywhere.** Every error response from every endpoint is RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` (see error-handling). An endpoint with its own error shape is a convention violation even if the shape is reasonable.

## BAN list

- **BAN-BE-011 — Verb in the URL.** Banned: paths that name operations instead of resources (`/getOrders`, `/createUser`, `/deleteItem`). Defeats: DET-CODE-014. Instead: model the resource — `POST /orders` creates, `GET /orders` lists, `DELETE /orders/{id}` removes (BE-023). Severity: WARN.
- **BAN-BE-012 — Error returned as 200.** Banned: a success status carrying an error body (`200 { "success": false, "error": "…" }`). Defeats: DET-CODE-022. Instead: return the decision-rule status with a problem-details body — `402`/`422` with `type`, `title`, and `detail` (BE-025, BE-030). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-BE-013 — Unbounded list endpoint.** Banned: a list endpoint that returns the whole collection with no pagination or maximum page size. Defeats: DET-CODE-033. Instead: paginate from day one with the API's one style and a capped page size (BE-026). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-BE-014 — Per-endpoint invention.** Banned: an endpoint that invents its own casing, pagination style, or filter grammar instead of following the convention sheet. Defeats: DET-CODE-014. Instead: follow the sheet (BE-021, BE-027); if the sheet is wrong, change the sheet and every endpoint together. Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-BE-011 — OpenAPI convention lint.** Verifies: BE-021, BE-022, BE-023, BE-027. Check: automated — run the OpenAPI linter (Spectral/Redocly) with the ruleset encoding the convention sheet over the API description in CI. Pass: zero lint errors. Fail: block merge. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-BE-012 — Status-code audit.** Verifies: BE-024, BE-025, BE-030. Check: automated — a script exercises create, delete, malformed-request, and business-rejection paths against a running instance and asserts the decision-rule status and a problem-details body for each. Pass: every sampled path returns the prescribed status and shape. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-BE-013 — New-endpoint convention review.** Verifies: BE-026, BE-028, BE-029. Check: manual — for each new or changed endpoint, diff its path, pagination, casing, and versioning against the convention sheet using the sheet's checklist. Pass: no unexplained deviation; a deliberate deviation updates the sheet in the same change. Fail: warn, and resolve before release. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- Paths name things; methods do the verbs.
- Errors are never 200.
- One pagination style, one casing, one grammar — from day one.
- Additive evolves; breaking versions.
- If it deviates, change the sheet and every endpoint together.

## Checklist

- [ ] The convention sheet exists and names its source guide (BE-021).
- [ ] OpenAPI lint with the convention ruleset is green in CI (G-BE-011).
- [ ] No path contains a verb; actions are sub-resources (BE-023).
- [ ] Sampled paths return decision-rule statuses with problem-details errors (G-BE-012).
- [ ] Every list endpoint paginates in the one style, with a max page size (BE-026).
- [ ] No released version was silently mutated; breaking changes follow BE-028.

<!-- generated from skills/backend/sdk-design/SKILL.md (bundle form) -->

# sdk-design

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D4 Backend & APIs (BE)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** Stripe, server-side SDKs (one API behavior, official SDKs in seven languages) — https://docs.stripe.com/sdks/server-side ; Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 — https://semver.org/ ; PROJECT_ANATOMY.md, "API implementation"
- **Depends on:** api-building, rest-conventions, error-handling
- **Feeds into:** sdk-embeddables, third-party-apis

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** building, generating, or reviewing a client library for an API you own — its models, client object, retry and timeout behavior, error types, versioning, and release packaging.
- **Do NOT use when:** designing the API itself (api-architecture, rest-conventions), consuming a third party's SDK (third-party-apis), or building embeddable widgets and scripts for other sites (sdk-embeddables). This skill governs libraries that wrap your own API.

## Rules

1. **BE-081 — One contract, two readers.** The SDK is generated from, or hand-maintained against, the same OpenAPI contract the server is contract-tested against. The SDK and the server may never be tested against different truths.
2. **BE-082 — Typed models for every resource.** Requests and responses are typed models mirroring the contract. The public surface never exposes untyped maps or raw JSON for a modeled resource.
3. **BE-083 — One client object.** A single client owns base URL, authentication, timeouts, and retries, configured once at construction. There are no global settings and no per-call surprises.
4. **BE-084 — Retries only where safe.** The SDK retries only idempotent operations, or requests carrying an idempotency key — and the same key is reused across retries. Attempts are bounded, with backoff.
5. **BE-085 — Timeouts are mandatory and configurable.** Every call has a timeout; the default is finite and documented, and the consumer can change it. An SDK call that can hang forever will.
6. **BE-086 — Errors are typed exceptions.** Failures surface as typed exceptions mapped from problem details, preserving status, problem `type`, and the correlation ID. Errors are never swallowed and never reduced to a bare string or a null.
7. **BE-087 — Semver, tracking the API major.** SDK versions follow Semantic Versioning and track the API major version they speak. A breaking SDK change is a major bump, whatever its size.
8. **BE-088 — Quickstart and changelog ship with every release.** The quickstart is runnable as written and completes the documented first task using only the README. Every release carries a changelog entry naming what changed.
9. **BE-089 — A raw escape hatch always exists.** Consumers can reach the underlying HTTP layer — custom path, headers, and body — for fields and endpoints the SDK has not modeled yet, without forking the library.
10. **BE-090 — Deprecations get a full cycle.** A deprecated method is announced in the changelog and marked in code (doc comment / deprecation attribute) for at least one minor cycle before removal, with the replacement named.

## BAN list

- **BAN-BE-041 — Silent retry of a non-idempotent call.** Banned: an SDK retry policy that replays POST creates (or other non-idempotent operations) on timeout or 5xx without an idempotency key. Defeats: DET-CODE-030. Instead: retry only idempotent operations, or attach one idempotency key at the first attempt and reuse it on every retry (BE-084). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-BE-042 — Swallowed errors.** Banned: SDK code that catches a failure and returns `null`, an empty object, or a default value, so the caller cannot tell failure from an empty result. Defeats: DET-CODE-005. Instead: throw the typed exception mapped from the problem-details response, with status and correlation ID intact (BE-086). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-BE-043 — Divergent hand-rolled behavior.** Banned: an SDK method that behaves differently from the raw API — extra defaults the server does not apply, business rules re-implemented client-side, responses transformed beyond the contract's mapping. Defeats: DET-CODE-027. Instead: the SDK is a faithful transport for the contract; rules live server-side, and any mapping the SDK performs is generated from the contract (BE-081). Severity: WARN.
- **BAN-BE-044 — No timeout.** Banned: shipping a client whose calls have no timeout, or a default of infinity, so a stalled server or network hangs the consumer's process indefinitely. Defeats: DET-CODE-006. Instead: set a finite documented default timeout on the client object, configurable per client and per call (BE-085). Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-BE-041 — Quickstart execution test.** Verifies: BE-088. Check: automated — in CI, create a clean project, install the SDK as a consumer would, and execute the README quickstart verbatim against a test instance. Pass: the documented first task completes with no undocumented step. Fail: block the release. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-BE-042 — SDK-vs-contract conformance run.** Verifies: BE-081, BE-082, BE-086. Check: automated — execute the API's contract test suite through the SDK instead of raw HTTP; assert identical statuses, shapes, and error mappings. Pass: the full suite green through the SDK. Fail: block the release. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-BE-043 — Retry-safety test.** Verifies: BE-084. Check: automated — against a stub server that commits a create and then drops the response, call the SDK's create method; assert exactly one server-side record exists afterward. Pass: one effect, whether the SDK declined to retry or reused its idempotency key. Fail: block the release. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-BE-044 — Timeout test.** Verifies: BE-085. Check: automated — point the SDK at a stub server that accepts the connection and never responds; assert the call fails with the typed timeout error within the configured bound plus tolerance. Pass: bounded failure with the typed error. Fail: block the release. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- The SDK and the server are tested against one contract.
- Retry only what is safe: idempotent, or keyed.
- No call hangs forever; every error is a typed exception.
- The quickstart is a test — if it doesn't run in CI, it's wrong.
- Semver, changelog, deprecation cycle: releases are a contract too.

## Checklist

- [ ] SDK models and behavior conform to the contract suite run through the SDK (G-BE-042).
- [ ] Retries are limited to idempotent operations or reuse one idempotency key (G-BE-043).
- [ ] Every call has a finite, configurable timeout (G-BE-044).
- [ ] Errors surface as typed exceptions preserving status, type, and correlation ID (BE-086).
- [ ] The README quickstart executes clean in a fresh project (G-BE-041).
- [ ] Version follows semver and tracks the API major; the changelog names the changes (BE-087, BE-088).
- [ ] A raw HTTP escape hatch exists for unmodeled fields (BE-089).

# user-reporting

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D4 Backend & APIs (BE)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** Trust & Safety Professional Association curriculum, content moderation simulation — https://www.tspa.org/curriculum/ts-curriculum/content-moderation-simulation/
- **Depends on:** api-building, backend-auth
- **Feeds into:** content-moderation, admin-tools

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** users can see or affect each other's content, accounts, or messages — every such surface needs a reporting intake whose records a moderation queue can actually work. This skill owns the intake and the record.
- **Do NOT use when:** the work is queue operations or enforcement policy itself — that is D7's content-moderation, consuming the records this skill creates. The staff surface that displays the queue is admin-tools. Do not substitute a contact form or a support inbox for a reporting channel.

## Rules

1. **BE-141 — A report is a record.** Every report action writes a structured record — reporter, target (content or account), category, context snapshot, timestamp — before any confirmation is shown to the reporter.
2. **BE-142 — In-product, per item.** Every user-generated surface offers a report action on the item and on the account. A generic contact page is not a reporting channel.
3. **BE-143 — The reporter stays anonymous.** The reported party never learns who reported them — not in a notification, not in an appeal, not in any surface.
4. **BE-144 — Severe categories jump the queue.** Child safety, credible threats, and illegal material route to the escalation path immediately, ahead of arrival order. Nothing severe waits behind spam flags.
5. **BE-145 — Every report reaches a decision.** A report moves through visible states (received → under review → decided) and cannot silently expire. Aging past the tier's SLA is surfaced by the queue-aging check, never absorbed quietly.
6. **BE-146 — Decisions cite policy.** Every enforcement action (label, reduce, remove, suspend, ban) records the policy clause it rests on, the deciding actor, and the timestamp.
7. **BE-147 — Actions are appealable.** The sanctioned user can appeal from the notice they receive; the appeal re-enters the queue as a fresh review of the same record.
8. **BE-148 — The reporter gets closure, not detail.** The reporter receives a received/decided signal. Enforcement specifics are never disclosed to the reporter.
9. **BE-149 — Reports are data.** Report records are queryable, so repeat-offender patterns and coordinated-reporting (brigading) patterns are computed from them. A sudden spike against one target is reviewed as a pattern before mass enforcement.
10. **BE-150 — Context is snapshotted.** The reported content is captured as it stood at report time. Editing or deleting the original afterward cannot erase the evidence under review.
11. **BE-151 — Intake validates the target.** The target is resolved and authorized server-side at intake: it must exist and be visible to the reporter. Reports against nonexistent or invisible targets are rejected, never queued.

## BAN list

- **BAN-BE-071 — The dead report button.** Banned: a report action that writes nothing, or sends an email to an unmonitored inbox, while showing "Thanks, we will review this." Defeats: DET-FAKE-015. Instead: persist the structured record (BE-141) and route it to the moderation queue before confirming to the reporter. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-BE-072 — Phantom enforcement.** Banned: marking a report "actioned — user banned" in the queue while no enforcement is applied to the account. Defeats: DET-FAKE-010. Instead: enforcement calls the same account service the product uses, and the report can close only after the account's new state is verified. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-BE-073 — Unvalidated report targets.** Banned: creating a report from a client-supplied target ID without verifying the target exists and is visible to the reporter. Defeats: DET-CODE-019. Instead: resolve and authorize the target server-side at intake (BE-151); reject what the reporter cannot see. Severity: WARN.
- **BAN-BE-074 — Silent report expiry.** Banned: reports auto-closing or dropping off the queue when they age, with no decision recorded. Defeats: DET-FAKE-011. Instead: undecided reports age into escalation (BE-145); a report leaves the queue only through a recorded decision. Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-BE-071 — End-to-end report trace.** Verifies: BE-141, BE-145, BE-146. Check: automated in staging — file a report as a test user, read the record back from the queue store, record a decision with a policy citation, and assert the reporter's closure signal exists. Pass: record, decision, citation, and closure all present. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-BE-072 — Forged-target rejection test.** Verifies: BE-151. Check: automated — submit reports against a random UUID and against a real record the reporter cannot see. Pass: both rejected, no queue records created. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-BE-073 — Queue-aging check.** Verifies: BE-145. Check: automated — seed staging with an undecided report older than its tier SLA and run the aging query. Pass: the report is flagged and escalated, not deleted or ignored. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-BE-074 — Severity-routing test.** Verifies: BE-144. Check: automated — file a spam report, then a child-safety report; read the escalation queue. Pass: the severe report is routed to escalation first, ahead of the earlier spam report. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- A report is a record, not an email.
- The reported party never learns who reported.
- Severe categories jump the queue, always.
- No decision without a policy citation.
- Every report ends decided — never expired, never deleted.

## Checklist

- [ ] Every user-generated surface has a per-item and per-account report action (BE-142).
- [ ] End-to-end report trace passes in staging (G-BE-071).
- [ ] Forged and invisible targets are rejected at intake (G-BE-072).
- [ ] Severe categories route to escalation immediately (G-BE-074).
- [ ] Decisions cite policy and sanctions are appealable (BE-146, BE-147).
- [ ] The reporter receives closure without enforcement detail (BE-148).
- [ ] The aging check flags overdue reports for escalation; none expire silently (G-BE-073).

# validation

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D4 Backend & APIs (BE)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** OWASP Input Validation Cheat Sheet — https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Input_Validation_Cheat_Sheet.html ; OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023) — https://orca.security/resources/blog/owasp-api-security-top-10/
- **Depends on:** api-architecture
- **Feeds into:** api-building, backend-auth, file-uploads

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** any data crosses a trust boundary into the server — request bodies, query and path parameters, headers, uploaded filenames, webhook payloads. If the server is about to trust it, store it, or act on it, this skill runs first.
- **Do NOT use when:** shaping URLs or status codes (rest-conventions), formatting the error response itself (error-handling), or checking who the caller is (backend-auth, rbac). Validation decides whether input is acceptable; it does not decide identity or permission.

## Rules

1. **BE-041 — Schema at the edge.** Every inbound payload — body, query, path, headers — is parsed through a declared schema (types, formats, lengths, ranges, allowlists, unknown-field policy) at the edge of the handler, before any business logic or persistence runs.
2. **BE-042 — Server-side always.** Browser or client validation is a UX aid, never a control. Every rule the client checks is checked again on the server; an endpoint that relies on the form is unvalidated.
3. **BE-043 — Allowlist over denylist.** Enumerate what is accepted. Write endpoints reject unknown fields outright, so extra properties in the body cannot be mass-assigned to the record (OWASP API3:2023, broken object property level authorization).
4. **BE-044 — Semantic checks follow syntactic ones.** After shape checks pass, verify meaning: date ranges are ordered, quantities are positive, and referenced objects exist and are visible to this caller.
5. **BE-045 — Validate the canonical form.** Decode first — URL encoding, Unicode normalization, path resolution — then validate the decoded value. A check against the raw string is bypassed by an alternate spelling of the same attack.
6. **BE-046 — Size before parse.** Body-size, field-count, and string-length caps run before schema work, so the validation layer itself cannot be exhausted by the payload it is checking.
7. **BE-047 — Failures are specific and total.** A failed validation returns `422` problem details listing each field and the rule it broke, and writes nothing — no partial record, no side effects, no queued jobs.
8. **BE-048 — Invariants live once, server-side.** A business rule (discount caps, eligibility, limits) is defined in exactly one server-side place. The client may mirror it for UX, but the server copy is the only enforcement.
9. **BE-049 — The schema is the contract schema.** The validation schema and the OpenAPI schema are one source, or are diffed in CI. Two hand-maintained copies will drift, and the drift is always in the permissive direction.
10. **BE-050 — Rejection is the safe default.** When a validator errors, times out, or meets a shape it does not recognize, the request is rejected. Validation never fails open.

## BAN list

- **BAN-BE-021 — Trusting the browser's validation.** Banned: a server endpoint that accepts and stores a payload because the shipped form checks it. Defeats: DET-CODE-019. Instead: parse every payload through the server-side schema at the handler's edge (BE-041, BE-042). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-BE-022 — Mass assignment.** Banned: binding the request body directly to a record (`create(req.body)`, `Object.assign(user, req.body)`) so client-sent fields like `isAdmin`, `role`, or `balanceCents` are persisted. Defeats: DET-FAKE-021. Instead: allowlist the writable fields in the schema and reject unknown fields on write endpoints (BE-043). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-BE-023 — Denylist as the only defense.** Banned: "validation" that string-matches known-bad fragments (`<script>`, `' OR 1=1`) instead of allowlisting shape and parameterizing queries. Defeats: DET-CODE-017. Instead: validate type and range against an allowlist schema, and bind values as parameters — never concatenate input into a query (BE-043). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-BE-024 — Duplicated rule, divergent constants.** Banned: the same business rule implemented independently on client and server with different values, so the layers disagree about what is allowed. Defeats: DET-CODE-027. Instead: define the invariant once server-side (BE-048); the client mirror is generated from, or tested against, that definition. Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-BE-021 — Boundary test pack.** Verifies: BE-041, BE-047, BE-050. Check: automated — for each endpoint, run the boundary pack: wrong types, oversized strings, missing required fields, inconsistent ranges, malformed encodings; assert `422` problem details and zero state change in the database after each case. Pass: every case rejected with no partial write. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-BE-022 — Schema-drift check.** Verifies: BE-049. Check: automated — diff the runtime validation schemas against the OpenAPI document in CI. Pass: zero differences. Fail: block merge. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-BE-023 — Mass-assignment probe.** Verifies: BE-043. Check: automated — send create/update requests carrying privileged extra fields (`role`, `isAdmin`, `ownerId`, `balanceCents`) and assert each is rejected or ignored and the stored record is unchanged in those fields. Pass: no privileged field is ever set from the request. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-BE-024 — Canonicalization probe.** Verifies: BE-045. Check: automated — submit encoded and alternate-spelling variants of rejected values (double-encoded traversal filenames, Unicode-confusable names, mixed-case injection strings) and assert the decoded form is what gets validated and rejected. Pass: every variant rejected. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- Nothing is trusted until the schema says so — server-side, at the edge.
- Allowlist what is accepted; reject what is unknown.
- Decode first, then validate the canonical form.
- A failed validation writes nothing.
- One invariant, one home: the server.

## Checklist

- [ ] Every payload (body, query, path, headers) passes a declared schema before business logic (BE-041).
- [ ] Write endpoints reject unknown fields; the mass-assignment probe passes (G-BE-023).
- [ ] Size and count caps run before schema parsing (BE-046).
- [ ] Validation failures return 422 problem details naming each field and rule, with zero state change (G-BE-021).
- [ ] Encoded/alternate spellings are validated in canonical form (G-BE-024).
- [ ] Validation schemas and the OpenAPI document diff clean in CI (G-BE-022).
- [ ] Business invariants exist in exactly one server-side place (BE-048).
